_national.labelling: Three classes: AOC (cantonal name or a defined area of a canton; "AOC" may abbreviate the term), vin de pays (country or part of it) and vin de table (only "suisse"; no origin, variety or vintage). Cantons set AOC rules: area, varieties, cultivation methods, minimum natural sugar per variety, maximum yield per variety, permitted winemaking, analysis and tasting. 63 AOC on the federal register (1 January 2026). Swiss wine may not be blended with foreign wine; AOC may be blended with up to 10% Swiss wine of the same colour (vin de pays 15%).
_national.min_alcohol: Federal AOC floors for natural sugar: whites 15.2 Brix (Suisse romande) or 15.8 Brix (German- and Italian-speaking Switzerland); reds 17.0 Brix (17.6 in Ticino and Mesolcina). Vin de pays: 14.4 Brix white, 15.2 red. Vin de table: 13.6 white, 14.4 red.
_national.max_yield: Federal AOC ceilings: white 1.4 kg/m2 (1.2 in Italian Switzerland), red 1.2 kg/m2; vin de pays 1.8 white, 1.6 red. Max 80 L wine per 100 kg grapes for AOC.
_national.ageing: Reserve/Riserva: AOC wine released after at least 18 months (red) or 12 months (white) of ageing counted from 1 October of the harvest year. Sur lie: aged on lees for at least one winter.
_national.sweetness: Sweetening of AOC wine is banned unless the canton allows it under federal food law. Specific terms: Selection de grains nobles/Beerenauslese at least 26.0 Brix, no enrichment; Eiswein/Vin de glace grapes frozen on the vine and picked at minus 7 C or below, at least 25.3 Brix; Fletri sur souche at least 13% potential, no additions; Trockenbeerenauslese at least 34.3 Brix; Vendange tardive/Spaetlese above the year's average sugar per cantonal rules; Passerille/Strohwein/Sforzato from dried grapes.
_national.other: Protected terms also include Oeil-de-Perdrix (rose from Pinot Noir, up to 10% Pinot Gris or Blanc), Schiller (red and white grapes from the same parcel vinified together), Federweiss/Weissherbst (German-speaking AOC from red grapes pressed early), Beerli (destemmed red), Primeur, Gletscherwein (Valais).

ch-geneve.max_yield: AOC Geneve: Chasselas and Riesling-Sylvaner 1.2 kg/m2, Gamay 1.1, others 1.0. Premier cru: Chasselas and Riesling-Sylvaner 1.0, others 0.9 kg/m2.
ch-geneve.labelling: Two AOC tiers: AOC Geneve (whole canton plus parts of neighbouring French communes) and the AOC Premier cru (mapped parcels of at least 1 ha, aspect between NE and NW via S; vinified and bottled in the canton; 75 cl and multiples or 50 cl). Communal name needs 85%. "Selection" needs 9 Oe above the AOC minimum; Reserve 18 months red / 12 months white; Vendange tardive picked 15 days after the usual date and 14 Oe above the cantonal average; Selection de grains nobles at least 110 Oe (26 Brix).

ch-valais.varieties: Many authorised; traditional names: Fendant (100% Chasselas, no additions), Johannisberg (Sylvaner), Malvoisie (Pinot Gris), Ermitage (Marsanne and/or Roussanne), Paien or Heida (Savagnin Blanc), Petite Arvine, Cornalin (Rouge du Pays), Dole (Pinot Noir alone or a red blend of at least 51% Pinot Noir and Gamay with Pinot Noir dominant), Oeil de Perdrix (Pinot Noir rose, up to 10% Pinot Gris/Blanc), Rose du Valais, Goron (VDP).
ch-valais.min_alcohol: AOC Valais natural sugar: Chasselas and other whites 17.2 Brix (70.6 Oe); Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc, Humagne Blanc, Reze 19.4 (80.3 Oe); Amigne, Arvine, Completer, Marsanne, Roussanne, Savagnin, Pinot Gris, Sylvaner 20.6 (85.6 Oe); all reds 20.0 (83.0 Oe). Sparkling base 17.2 Brix. The department may lower minima in difficult years. Grand Cru: Chasselas 18.8 (77.6 Oe); Humagne Blanc, Reze 20.6 (85.6); Amigne, Arvine, Marsanne, Roussanne, Pinot Gris, Savagnin, Sylvaner 22.6 (94.6); Pinot Noir 22.0 (91.9); Cornalin, Gamay, Humagne Rouge, Syrah 21.2 (88.3); vin surmature 30.2 (130 Oe); no lowering.
ch-valais.max_yield: AOC: Chasselas 1.4 kg/m2, other whites and reds 1.2 kg/m2 (the Interprofession may adjust by up to 0.4 kg/m2). Vin de pays with traditional name 1.6 kg/m2. Grand Cru: Chasselas 1.1, Sylvaner 1.0, others 0.8 kg/m2.
ch-valais.labelling: Classes renamed: AOC (former category I), vin de pays (former II), vin de table (former III). Grand Cru is communal or regional, defined by a commune regulation approved by the State Council; only with the commune or region name ("Grand Cru Valais" banned; "premier cru", "cru classe", "grand cru du Valais" etc. prohibited); vintage mandatory.
ch-valais.other: Grand Cru varieties: Chasselas (Fendant), Sylvaner, Amigne, Arvine, Marsanne, Roussanne, Savagnin (Heida), Humagne Blanc, Pinot Gris (Malvoisie), Reze; Pinot Noir, Gamay, Cornalin, Humagne Rouge, Syrah. Vines at least 8 years old; vinified and bottled in Valais; no blending (except surmature and Dole Grand Cru), no vintage blending, no sweetening. Cornalin, Humagne Rouge and Syrah Grand Cru not released before 1 April of the second year. Vin surmature requires drying on the vine and no enrichment.

ch-vaud.varieties: Chasselas dominant; unnamed white AOC must be at least 90% Chasselas. Single variety 85%; each named variety at least 15% and named varieties at least 85% together.
ch-vaud.min_alcohol: Natural sugar: Chablais and Lavaux whites 15.9 Brix (65 Oe), Gamay 17.0 (70 Oe), other reds 18.2 (75 Oe); La Cote, Cotes-de-l'Orbe, Bonvillars whites 15.7 (64 Oe). Dezaley and Calamin Grand cru: whites 17.3 (71 Oe), Gamay 19.3 (80 Oe), other reds 20.5 (85 Oe).
ch-vaud.styles: Traditional names: Dorin (Vaud Chasselas meeting AOC sugar minima) and Salvagnin (Vaud red, also Salvagnin rose). Oeil de Perdrix: Pinot Noir rose with up to 10% Pinot Gris or Blanc.
ch-vaud.ageing: Reserve: released after 18 months (red) or 12 months (white) from 1 October of harvest; "Grande reserve" not allowed. Selection de grains nobles at least 26.0 Brix (110 Oe); Vendanges tardives picked at least 14 days after the usual date; Vin doux naturel 15 to 22%.
ch-vaud.labelling: AOC regions: Chablais, Lavaux, La Cote, Cotes-de-l'Orbe, Bonvillars, Vully (shared with Fribourg), Dezaley Grand cru, Calamin Grand cru (and Dezaley-Marsens Grand cru). Lieu de production needs 60% from it (40% from the same region). "Grand cru": at least 90% from the named lieu or commune, 5 Oe above the region's minimum, no blending, vintage mandatory. "Premier grand cru": parcel-level award by a commission; Chasselas, Pinot Noir, Gamay, Merlot, Gamaret, Garanoir; at least 6,000 vines/ha, hand harvest, max 0.80 L/m2 (Chasselas) or 0.64 L/m2 (reds), Chasselas at least 75 Oe, Gamay 80, other reds 85; no blending; vinified and bottled in Vaud in Vaud-shaped bottles; vintage mandatory.
ch-vaud.other: Enrichment max +2.5% vol (whites to 14.5%, reds and roses to 15%); oak chips and sweetening banned on AOC. Irrigation banned after veraison. Blending banned for AOC Lavaux.
